9703.t: Feminine adjective, from Ἕλλην (Héllēn, “Greek”) + -ις (-ĭs, feminine suffix).

9705.t: Uncertain origin; usually linked to ἕρμα (hérma, “heap of stones”), itself of non-Indo-European substrate origin or from Proto-Indo-European *ser- (“to bind, put together”). Beekes suggests a Pre-Greek origin.

9777.t: Etymology tree the BMAC substratebor.? Proto-Indo-Iranian *síndʰuš ▲ Proto-Indo-Iranian *síndʰuš Sanskrit सिन्धु॑ (síndhu)bor. Old Persian 𐏃𐎡𐎯𐎢𐏁 (hiⁿdūš)bor.

9711.t: From Proto-Hellenic *auhṓs, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂éwsōs (“dawn”), which was also personified as a goddess of dawn in Proto-Indo-European religion, corresponding to Ancient Greek goddess Ἠώς (Ēṓs).

9709.t: From Proto-Hellenic *wākʰā́, from Proto-Indo-European *sweh₂gʰ- (“to sound”). Cognate with Old English swōgan (“to resound”).

9706.t: From ἠθολόγος (ēthológos, “painting manners or character by mimic gestures”) from ἦθος (êthos, “character”) + λόγος (lógos, “account”).

9744.t: No etymology. Furnée connects the word with ἰξύς (ixū́s, “loins”) assuming a common Pre-Greek origin.

9772.t: Perhaps a nominal formation from ἴλλω (íllō, “to press together”), from Proto-Indo-European *wi-wl-e, a reduplicative formation from Proto-Indo-European *wel- (“to press together”), whence also εἴλω (eílō, “to shut in, press”); see there for more discussion.

9784.t: Perhaps from the same root as ὀδύνη (odúnē, “pain”).

9735.t: A hypostasis *ἐν-γνύ-α (*en-gnú-a, “place in the knee”). The stem ἰγνύς (ignús) was formed after ἰξύς (ixús, “waist, loins”) and ὀσφῦς (osphûs, “hips or loins”).

9783.t: From ὀγδοήκοντα (ogdoḗkonta, “eighty”) + -στός (-stós), a variant of -τός (-tós, ordinal suffix).

9733.t: From ἰατρεύω (īātreúō, “to treat medically, to cure”) + -εῖον (-eîon).
